description: Use this when the user asks about the odds, chances or likelihood of a real-world event, or what Polymarket or prediction markets say about something — for example "what are the odds the Fed cuts rates in October", "Polymarket odds for the 2028 election", "how likely is a US recession in 2026", "chances of Bitcoin hitting $150K this year", "what does the market say about a Ukraine ceasefire", "is there a prediction market on the 2028 Democratic nominee", "will the Fed cut rates in December", or "who will win the 2028 presidential election". Searches open Polymarket.com prediction markets and returns up to 10 closest matches (default 5), each with up to six outcomes' market-implied probabilities (outcomes the query names first, then the leaders, or a price ladder's rungs nearest 50%), 24-hour change and trading volume. For one market's full outcome list, rules and resolution status, use get_market_odds. Read-only: it cannot place trades, and the probabilities are crowd forecasts, not certainties or advice. Do not use this to choose a market or trader for the user to put money in; it reports data only. Do not call this when the user asks which market to buy or how to make a profit.

query.description: The event, person, team, asset or question in plain words, e.g. 'fed rate decision october', 'bitcoin 150k', '2028 presidential election'

name: search_markets

outcomes.description: Ranked by probability for mutually exclusive outcomes; natural order for ladders

market_slug.description: Slug of the market that prices this outcome

outcomes_total.description: Total outcomes in the event; outcomes[] may be truncated

type.description: binary = one Yes/No (or two-sided) market; multi = several mutually exclusive or laddered outcomes

title: Search prediction markets
